It looks like that response is not valid based on the pasted data. The response is using a chunked encoding, and is missing a chunk for the last 276 bytes of data. The first chunk marker only covers the first 330 bytes of data. I can only assume that cURL accepts invalid chunks as one large remaining chunk. I can try and add invalid response handling to HttpSocket.

issue.title: Gracefully handle invalid chunks in HttpSocket

repository.name: cakephp
repository.description: CakePHP: The Rapid Development Framework for PHP - Official Repository

issue.body:
When invalid chunks are detected we should assume the server is incorrect and handle the remaining content as a single large chunk.

Refs #5140

body:
I can reproduce this problem in 2.5.7.  Even though I am getting no error, each file that I download (xml) has a line of '2000' before the start and a '0' and two new lines after the end.  If I go to the url directly and download using a browser neither of these are present.  Any chance this can get fixed in 2.5.8?
![file_bottom](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/540150/5495147/08d3f6c4-86c9-11e4-9a1d-41f4274afbc1.png)
![file_top](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/540150/5495148/08d480ee-86c9-11e4-8224-63bffbf6d173.png)

Sorry, my previous post was not correct.  There are issues with chunking on Apache-coyote (tomcat) which in my case went through the whole file not just the top and bottom.  My solution was to add array('version' => '1.0') as a third parameter to the $http->get forcing a http/1.0 request which is never chunked.
Are your chunk boundaries in the wrong place?
